section_summary: The section opens with cross-reference notes on exhibitions in Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka, Nagoya and New York. Most pages concern the proposed 1937 Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition: Japanese organizers seek United States participation, while the State Department concludes that official participation is unlikely and asks federal departments to publicize the event. Consular reports, replies and exhibitor instructions document the exhibition’s plans, costs and shipping arrangements.

subfiles.title: Report excerpt on the proposed Siamese Exposition
subfiles.about: Reviews press reports and questions the announced opening date.
subfiles.summary: Press accounts named Prince Chichibu as patron, but the writer doubts the March 15 date because of the Siamese king’s travel schedule.

subfiles.title: Japanese response to the World Two-Way Fair
subfiles.about: Reports why Yokohama business interests declined to join the New York fair.
subfiles.summary: The Yokohama chamber declined to participate. Boyce says local firms favored fairs in Japan and would need convincing evidence of commercial benefit before joining an overseas fair.

subfiles.title: Invitation to the Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition
subfiles.from: Charles H. Stephan, American Vice Consul, Nagoya
subfiles.about: Transmits exhibition pamphlets and conveys Nagoya’s request for active United States participation.
subfiles.summary: Stephan describes the city’s planned March–May 1937 exhibition, his remarks at a preliminary meeting, and Nagoya’s hope for an American building and exhibits. He reports that space would be free, while construction costs would fall to the United States or exhibitors; reduced freight rates and customs concessions were expected.

subfiles.about: Forwards Stephan’s despatch for preliminary consideration.
subfiles.summary: Asks Agriculture to consider participation pending a formal Japanese invitation.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Vice Consul Stephan
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, Department of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Stephan’s Nagoya exhibition despatch.
subfiles.summary: Says interested departments have received copies for consideration.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of Nagoya plans
subfiles.about: Acknowledges early notice of the Nagoya exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Treasury can plan its role if a federal exhibit is authorized.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of Nagoya plans
subfiles.about: Promises departmental consideration of federal participation.
subfiles.summary: Commerce bureaus will assess representation while awaiting a formal invitation.

subfiles.title: Embassy copy of reply to Nagoya
subfiles.about: Sends the Embassy a copy of State’s reply to Nagoya.
subfiles.summary: Completes the Embassy’s record of Stephan’s despatch.

subfiles.title: Japanese foreign minister’s Nagoya invitation
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a Japanese Foreign Office note urging United States participation.
subfiles.summary: Neville reports that the exhibition marks the thirtieth anniversary of Nagoya port’s opening to international trade. The foreign minister requests an early answer about American participation.

subfiles.title: Foreign Minister Hirota’s invitation
subfiles.about: Asks Neville to urge United States participation in Nagoya.
subfiles.summary: Hirota conveys the promoters’ request and seeks an early answer for exhibit-space planning.

subfiles.title: Agriculture’s response on Nagoya participation
subfiles.about: Offers conditional support for a government exhibit.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture favors participation if Congress authorizes it, citing Nagoya’s industry and Japan’s cotton market.

subfiles.title: Interior’s response on Nagoya participation
subfiles.from: Charles West, Acting Secretary of the Interior
subfiles.about: Offers conditional Interior Department participation.
subfiles.summary: Interior would contribute if funding becomes available.

subfiles.title: Embassy copy of reply to Nagoya
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the reply to Stephan.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the instruction on page 29.

subfiles.title: Closing page of instruction on Nagoya participation
subfiles.about: Directs distribution of an instruction concerning exhibition publicity.
subfiles.summary: The surviving closing page asks that copies be sent to the Nagoya consul.

subfiles.title: Revised Nagoya guidance to Labor
subfiles.about: Explains why official United States participation is unlikely.
subfiles.summary: State interprets Hirota’s note as an invitation on behalf of promoters, not an official Japanese government invitation. It recommends publicity so private Americans may consider exhibiting.

subfiles.title: Revised Nagoya guidance to Agriculture
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains the distinction between a promoters’ invitation and an official invitation.
subfiles.summary: State says federal participation is improbable and recommends publicity for possible private exhibitors.

subfiles.title: Revised Nagoya guidance to Commerce
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests Commerce publicity for the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: State says the promoters’ invitation does not amount to an official Japanese government invitation and federal participation is improbable.

subfiles.title: Revised Nagoya guidance to Interior
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests Interior publicity for the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: State explains its view of the promoters’ invitation and the unlikely prospect of official participation.

subfiles.title: Revised Nagoya guidance to Treasury
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains the revised position on official participation.
subfiles.summary: State recommends publicity for private exhibitors while advising that official United States participation is unlikely.

subfiles.title: Commerce agrees to publicize Nagoya
subfiles.about: Confirms Commerce will publicize the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will use Commerce Reports and its offices across the United States.

subfiles.title: Agriculture agrees to publicize Nagoya
subfiles.about: Offers customary publicity and requests further despatches.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture will publicize the exposition through its usual channels.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy discussion of Nagoya plans
subfiles.about: Records Hayama’s presentation of exhibition material.
subfiles.summary: Hayama independently urged American government participation and left a memorandum and pamphlets.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy memorandum on Nagoya
subfiles.about: Urges United States support for the Nagoya exhibition.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy describes the exhibition’s aims of displaying Pacific nations’ industry and culture and promoting peace. It asks the United States Government to help secure broad participation.

subfiles.title: Embassy reports its reply to Hirota
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports delivery of the United States response to the invitation.
subfiles.summary: Neville says the Embassy told the Foreign Office that official participation was improbable, while American departments were asked to publicize the exposition. He encloses the note.

subfiles.title: American reply to Foreign Minister Hirota
subfiles.about: States the United States position on participation.
subfiles.summary: Neville says official government participation is improbable but appropriate departments will publicize the exposition.

subfiles.title: Prince Higashikuni becomes exhibition governor
subfiles.from: Charles H. Stephan, American Consulate, Nagoya
subfiles.about: Reports stronger Japanese government backing for the exposition.
subfiles.summary: Prince Higashikuni was inaugurated as exhibition governor. Japan’s commerce minister and a Foreign Office representative announced government approval, support and active participation, apparently addressing earlier doubts about official Japanese involvement.

subfiles.title: Directions to Exhibitors transmitted

subfiles.summary: Transmits printed exhibitor directions and promises further maps and plans.

subfiles.title: Directions to Exhibitors transmitted: copy

subfiles.title: The Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition: Directions to Exhibitors
subfiles.about: Sets out practical rules and charges for exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: The circular lists space rents, packing and shipment requirements, freight discounts, customs treatment, exhibit removal rules and construction costs. It names shipping lines and gives exchange rates and miscellaneous charges.

subfiles.title: Agriculture’s reply on exhibitor publicity
subfiles.about: Offers limited publicity for the exhibitor circular.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture will help, though Commerce has more relevant contacts.

subfiles.title: Commerce’s reply on exhibitor publicity
subfiles.about: Promises to share the exhibitor information.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will make the circular available to interested contacts.

subfiles.title: Interior’s reply on exhibitor publicity
subfiles.about: Promises distribution and publicity for the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Interior will distribute the pamphlets and publicize Nagoya.

subfiles.title: Nagoya exhibition posters and revised budget
subfiles.from: Charles H. Stephan, American Consulate, Nagoya
subfiles.about: Transmits exhibition posters and updates financing and recruitment plans.
subfiles.summary: Stephan sends bird’s-eye-view posters, reports that the budget rose to 3.7 million yen with a 100,000-yen central government grant, and says Nagoya’s mayor plans to solicit participation in American Pacific coast cities.

subfiles.title: Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition publicity text
subfiles.about: Promotes Nagoya’s industry, port development and the exhibition’s peace aims.
subfiles.summary: The visible page links Nagoya’s industrial growth and new facilities to the planned 1937 exhibition.
